title: Implement Jira migration command
description: Once the Atlassian MCP server is registered in `.claude/settings.json` and credentials are configured, add a one-shot command that walks every task file with `jira_key: null`, creates the matching Jira issue, and writes the returned issue key back to the JSON. After migration, the local store becomes an append-only audit log and Jira is the source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: Command is idempotent: re-running it never creates duplicate Jira issues.
Field mapping is one-to-one with no data loss for: title, description, acceptance_criteria (rendered into the Jira description), priority, labels, status (mapped to the matching Jira workflow state).
Each migrated task gets `jira_key` populated and `updated_at` refreshed.
A dry-run flag prints the planned migrations without calling Jira.

comments.author: researcher
comments.body: DEEP-RESEARCH RESULT (run wf_395849ee-f0a, 2026-06-12, /deep-research workflow — first live research run, doubling as TASK-038 UAT). KEY FACTS (all high-confidence, sourced): (1) Official path = Atlassian Rovo MCP Server, GA 2026-02-04, hosted gateway for Jira+Confluence under existing user permissions. (2) ENDPOINT: https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp (OAuth variant /v1/mcp/authv2); legacy /v1/sse UNSUPPORTED after 2026-06-30 — configure the /mcp endpoint, the old SSE one dies in ~2 weeks. (3) Auth: browser OAuth 2.1 w/ dynamic client registration, OR org-admin-enabled API tokens (Basic base64(email:token) or service-account Bearer in mcp.json headers). (4) Auth choice constrains tool surface: JSM/Bitbucket tools = API-token-only; Compass = OAuth-only. (5) Jira tools in admin-granted permission groups: read_jira (getJiraIssue, getTransitionsForJiraIssue, getVisibleJiraProjects, lookupJiraAccountId), write_jira (createJiraIssue, editJiraIssue, addCommentToJiraIssue, transitionJiraIssue, addWorklogToJiraIssue), search_jira (searchJiraIssuesUsingJql) — full issue CRUD + comments + transitions, mapping ~1:1 onto our task-store/MCP surface. (6) Three gating layers must all pass: admin domain allowlist, org IP allowlist, app permissions. GAPS the run flagged for the researcher to close before implementation: alternatives comparison (open-source mcp-atlassian, thin REST v3 wrapper) lost to result truncation; transition IDs vs status names unconfirmed (load-bearing for our transitionStatus mapping); ADF vs markdown for comment bodies; whether subagents inherit MCP tool access in Claude Code; OAuth-in-headless behavior; single-source dates need cross-checking. Full result: session transcript wf_395849ee-f0a.
